source: Xiong et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior
finding: Agents copy retrieved experiences when the new task looks like an old one, so wrong stored cases propagate (error propagation). Adding every run to memory is worse than a small fixed memory. A strict quality check on what is added is best. Deleting low-value records can beat an error-free memory.
numbers: Final scores, fixed memory / add-all / strict add: RegAgent SR 67.53 / 55.48 / 70.95; EHRAgent ACC 16.75 / 13.05 / 38.50; AgentDriver SR 40.11 / 32.32 / 51.00; CIC-IoT (network-traffic diagnosis) ACC 71.50 / 59.90 / 85.40. History deletion with strict check: CIC-IoT 85.40 to 89.60 with memory 904 to 788. Combined deletion: 904 to 188 records at 85.50. Input-output similarity correlation near r=1 on RegAgent. GPT-4o-mini backbone.
quote: indiscriminate addition will easily introduce incorrect executions
limits: Not a troubleshooting benchmark except CIC-IoT classification. Read through a WebFetch summary of the HTML, first 100k characters. Strict = ground-truth check; coarse = LLM judge. Table 1 and 2 baselines differ slightly.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for gaps 5 and 2: noisy cases hurt (add-all lost 5 to 12 points vs fixed memory). A case bank needs an admission gate and pruning.

source: Cloud-OpsBench (2026) A Reproducible Benchmark for Agentic Root Cause Analysis in Cloud Systems, Tables 6 and 7
finding: Re-opened. Three retrieved GPT-5 success trajectories (ICL) raised accuracy on OnlineBoutique for all three models but not on TrainTicket, where two of three models got worse. Category runbook (SOP) gave little and hurt Qwen on OnlineBoutique. Token cost of ICL and SOP was NOT reported. No abstain rule tested.
numbers: OnlineBoutique JRA mean base 0.70, ICL 0.79, SOP 0.71; ECR 0.62, 0.75, 0.64. TrainTicket JRA 0.58, ICL 0.56, SOP 0.60. Per model TrainTicket JRA base to ICL: DeepSeek-V4-Flash 0.63 to 0.55, Qwen3.5-27B 0.58 to 0.54, Gemini-2.5-Flash 0.53 to 0.58. Qwen OnlineBoutique SOP 0.70 to 0.63. Harness tokens per case (GLM-5.1): ReAct 55.13K OB / 129.46K TT; Reflection 76.82K / 230.78K with JRA 0.84 vs 0.81 OB and 0.57 vs 0.55 TT; Codex 126.29K / 205.17K.
limits: Experience pool comes from a stronger model (GPT-5), one run per cell; differences of 0.03 to 0.08 may be noise. Read via WebFetch of the first 100k of 156k characters.
agent_relevance: Gap 1: no equal-token test exists, but the harness table shows more tokens (Reflection, Codex) buy little on TrainTicket. Gap 2: harm is real (about -0.04 to -0.08 JRA on the harder system).

source: Compliance Trap (2026) Diagnosing How AI Agents Consume Conflicting Memory
finding: Plausible but task-wrong memory is followed at the first step in about two thirds of runs and hurts a lot. Agents rarely recover after diverging. A verify-first warning cuts damage but also cuts the benefit of correct memory. Relevance gating gave no consistent gain. Abstention was not tested. Adding helpful memory only after a failed run was the best schedule.
numbers: Compliance with memory advice at step 1 on WebArena: 63 to 72 percent across 5 models. WebArena (77-task subset) no memory vs conflicting memory: Qwen3.5-27B 49.0 to 23.5; Gemini-3-Flash 46.3 to 27.8; Gemma-4-26B 38.1 to 30.9; Qwen3.5-9B 26.4 to 17.0. MemTrapBench (231 tasks): conflicting memory leaves 1.3 to 6.9 percent (damage 9.5 to 26.0 points) while helpful memory adds 25.5 to 30.7 points. Re-alignment after divergence 7 to 15 percent for conflicting vs 27 to 42 percent for helpful. Verify-warning: damage cut 17.2, gain cut 11.0 points (Qwen3.5-27B). Retry-on-fail: +10.4 on WebArena vs +1.3 always-on.
limits: Web agents with injected text, not diagnosis. WebArena subset was chosen because memory changed outcomes, so effects are inflated. Gemini coverage inconsistent in the paper. Absolute MemTrapBench values were derived by the summariser from deltas.
agent_relevance: Core evidence for gap 2: the harm when the retrieved case is wrong is large (10 to 25 points). A bank without a match-quality check is dangerous; a use-memory-only-after-failure schedule is a cheap design.

source: Boundary-Calibrated Intervention Transfer (2026) Knowing When Not to Reuse: Conditional Experience Transfer in Autonomous LLM Post-Training
finding: A gate that rejects or validates past experience before reuse removes most harmful reuse while keeping most helpful reuse. This is the closest direct test of abstain-on-poor-match, but it is about training updates, not case retrieval in a prompt.
numbers: Audit of 24 past candidates (10 beneficial, 8 harmful, 6 neutral): reuse-all authorises 8 of 8 harmful (100 percent); Flat-Additive 5 of 8 (62.5); gate (BCIT) 2 of 8 (25.0) while keeping 9 of 10 beneficial (90 percent); abstains on about 41.7 percent. Cross-task mean score: base 42.5, reuse-all 42.5 (worst delta -1.4), BCIT 47.0 (worst +3.6); BCIT vs flat +2.63, CI 2.10 to 3.16. Qwen3-4B, 6 paired seeds. McNemar BCIT vs flat p=.25 on the audit.
limits: Different object (fine-tuning updates, Qwen3-4B). Audit of 24 is small. Abstention rates are derived by the summariser.
agent_relevance: Supports the idea that a gate cuts negative transfer; a prompt-time version for diagnosis cases is untested (gap 2 stays open for diagnosis).

source: MemTransfer (2026) Benchmarking Memory Beyond Matched Experience in Embodied Decision-Making
finding: Memory that works when the case matches exactly falls hard when the start or route differs. Retrieval over raw episodes scales with more stored demos; summaries and semantic rules do not.
numbers: Warehouse navigation, 100 cases, 6 memory types, one frozen VLM. Original start, 1 demo: Episodic 100.0, Full-context 95.3, Summary 43.0, no memory 0.8. New start: Episodic 51.7 (1 demo) to 66.0 (4 demos), Full-context 46.7 to 48.0, Summary 44.3 to 44.0, Semantic 19.7 to 17.0. Blocked route: Episodic 37.0, retention 0.56. Loss about 48 to 49 points at new start.
limits: Embodied navigation, not diagnosis. No gating tested; authors list selective use as future work.
agent_relevance: Gaps 7 and 4: gain from more cases depends on retrieval over raw episodes, not on summaries; exact-match success overstates transfer by about 50 points.

source: Escaping the Self-Confirmation Trap (2026) Execute-Distill-Verify for Agentic Experience Learning
finding: Stored lessons that rationalise an execution error are common even in strong memory methods, and they hurt. Verifying each lesson before storing removes most of them. It is also a third-party run of ReasoningBank on other benchmarks: the gain was small there.
numbers: tau2-bench average Pass@1 (MiniMax-M2.1): no memory 76.4, self-reflection 77.7, ReasoningBank 79.0, ReasoningBank with scaling 82.3, EDV 86.6. Wrong-but-consistent lesson rate, Retail subset: self-reflection 22.0, ReasoningBank 16.0, RB scaling 11.0, EDV 5.0 percent. Paired test, 60 runs per cell: original wrong lesson task success 40.0, lesson removed 55.0, lesson corrected 65.0. Verifier keeps 68 percent of candidates at 96.5 percent precision, rejects 88 percent of bad ones. ReasoningBank score fell from 82.5 (1 item) to 79.3 (3 items) with GLM-4.7.
limits: Tool-use dialogue and web tasks, not diagnosis. 60 runs are not 60 independent tasks. Authors propose EDV, so a competing-method bias is possible.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 partly (RB +2.6 on tau2 vs about +8 in its own paper on WebArena) and gap 5: a wrong lesson costs 15 to 25 points of task success. Add a verify step before a case enters the bank.

source: Evo-Memory (2025) Benchmarking LLM Agent Test-time Learning with Self-Evolving Memory
finding: Retrieving past experience (ExpRAG) helps multi-step tasks a lot on both models; a reason-act-refine memory (ReMem) helps more. Gain is larger when tasks in the stream are similar. Unfiltered failed trajectories hurt the simple retrieval baseline. Gains on single-turn reasoning are small. ExpeL and ReasoningBank are not in the paper.
numbers: Multi-turn avg success, no memory / ExpRAG / ReMem: Gemini-2.5-Flash 0.27 / 0.46 / 0.50; Claude 3.7 Sonnet 0.24 / 0.63 / 0.78. Single-turn avg: Gemini 0.59 / 0.60 / 0.65; Claude 0.54 / 0.59 / 0.58. BabyAI got worse with memory for Gemini (0.61 to 0.56). Noisy stream (success/progress): ExpRAG 0.38 / 0.69 vs ReMem 0.54 / 0.76 (Gemini). Gain correlated with task similarity r=0.717 (Gemini) and 0.563 (Claude). Top-k=4 BGE retriever.
limits: Authors are from Google, as is ReasoningBank, so not fully independent. The summariser found internal inconsistencies in the paper. Read first 100k of 113k characters.
agent_relevance: Gap 7: gains grow with similarity of stored and new tasks; fits a repeat-fault bank, weaker on novel faults.

source: EvoMemBench (2026) Benchmarking Agent Memory from a Self-Evolving Perspective
finding: Independent comparison of 15 memory methods including AWM, ReasoningBank and AgentKB. No method wins everywhere. A strong long-context model with no memory often beats every memory method. Memory methods often cost 2 to 4 times the tokens.
numbers: Backbone DeepSeek-V3.2. In-episode execution (success) at 16K/32K/64K/128K: no memory 28.5/35.5/45.3/39.5; ReasoningBank 43.0/49.5/47.1/48.0; AWM 31.5/43.0/53.1/35.0; Gemini-3-Flash without memory 50.5/65.5/66.9/62.0. Cross-episode knowledge: GPT-5-mini without memory (Easy 60.8, Medium 21.6, Hard 14.4) beats every memory method. Tokens CrossEp-Tool: DeepSeek 55,787 vs BM25 202,966 vs A-MEM 181,298.
limits: General agent tasks, no fault diagnosis. Truncated page; some tables unread. ExpeL and Memento not tested. The GPT-5-mini comparison was made by the summariser, not the authors.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: first independent run of ReasoningBank and AWM (positive for execution, uneven for knowledge). Gap 1: at equal tokens a stronger base model beats memory in many cells.

source: Agent KB (2025) Leveraging Cross-Domain Experience for Agentic Problem Solving
finding: Shared experience store with a plan-stage and a feedback-stage retrieval. Both stages help; auto-built experiences nearly match hand-written ones; but retrieved knowledge hurt in some cells.
numbers: GAIA with smolagents GPT-4.1 pass@1: baseline 55.15, full 61.21, no planning step 59.39, no feedback step 59.39, no retrieve module 57.58, raw workflow 58.18. Hand-crafted knowledge GAIA 76.97, SWE-bench Lite 55.67; auto 75.15 and 51.00; none 55.15 and 24.33. Harm: OWL GPT-4o GAIA L3 30.8 to 23.1 (-7.7).
limits: Authors' own method. Disagreement-gate benefit shown only in a figure with no numbers. Not diagnosis.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: automatic cases are about as good as expert ones (1.8 to 4.7 points less); gap 2: even a gated store showed a -7.7 cell.

source: Hernandez-Serrano and Jonassen (2003) The effects of case libraries on problem solving, Journal of Computer Assisted Learning 19(1)
finding: Undergraduates solving ill-structured food-product-development problems. Experimental group read stories of similar solved problems, comparison group read summaries, control read unrelated text. Experimental group scored higher on multiple-choice questions about problem-solving processes; short-answer showed no significant difference. Abstract only; no means or sample size were available.
numbers: Three groups; MC test significant for experimental; short-answer not significant (authors suggest test fatigue). No N or effect size obtained.
limits: Only the CrossRef abstract and the ERIC record were read; full text not opened. Food product development, not fault diagnosis. Outcome was knowledge of process, not solving real faults.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: the foundational case-library result is weak and far from diagnosis. Do not cite it as evidence that cases improve diagnosis performance.

source: Tawfik and Jonassen (2013); Tawfik (2017) Do Cases Teach Themselves; Tawfik, Sanchez and Saparova (2014); Tawfik, Kim and Kim (2020); Tawfik et al. (2019, 2020) ERIC records
finding: A set of studies from one lab. Failure cases beat success cases on counterarguments and holistic argumentation (N=36), also in a transfer case one week later without the library. Retrieval/reuse prompts did worse than no prompts or retain prompts. A recommendation-system library beat a static library on rebuttals. A case-library group collaborated more (N=22). A later paper found no group difference in understanding the problem space between success and failure cases.
numbers: Tawfik and Jonassen 2013: N=36. Tawfik 2017: no-prompt and retain-prompt groups beat retrieval/reuse group on counterclaim and holistic scores. Tawfik 2014: N=22. Tawfik 2019 (success vs failure cases in collaboration): failure group better on conceptual understanding, no difference in problem space. Tawfik, Hung and Giabbanelli 2020: N=91, PBL vs lecture vs case-based, PBL best on conceptual knowledge.
limits: Read as ERIC record descriptions only (paraphrased), not full papers. All from Tawfik's group; argumentation tasks, not fault diagnosis. Small N, no effect sizes obtained.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: no replication outside Tawfik/Jonassen found for these; gap 5: failure cases may help human novices, but the 2019 null on problem space limits it. Prompting people to retrieve and reuse can backfire; the LLM analogue is over-eager copying.

source: Park, Park, Jung and Kim (2020) Promoting Case Indexing in Case Library Learning: Effects of Indexing Prompts on Self-Explanation and Problem Solving
finding: Independent group, 105 students over three course sections. Explanation-based indexing prompts and difference-based indexing prompts both raised self-explanation and both beat the control on rebuttals. The only non-Tawfik human case-library test found, and it tests indexing (gap 4) directly.
numbers: N=105 in 3 sections; both prompt types above no prompt on rebuttals; exact means not obtained.
limits: ERIC description only. Section-level assignment may confound class and condition. Career-development course, not troubleshooting.
agent_relevance: Gaps 4 and 8: indexing a case by why it matters (explanation) or how it differs helps; supports a bank record that carries a cause and a difference note, not only symptom text.

source: When Continual Learning Moves to Memory (2026) A Study of Experience Reuse in LLM Agents
finding: Raw trajectories can cause negative transfer on harder target tasks; abstract insights transfer better. How insights are indexed (bundled top-1 vs separate top-3) changes results by environment, and a sparse index can send 88.5 percent of queries to one item.
numbers: Qwen-Plus, ReMe memory, BM25. Forward transfer, ALFWorld A to B: raw -9.5, insight +6.5; BabyAI A to B: raw -7.5, insight +9.0. Hard-case no-loss delta: raw -26.1 (ALFWorld). Per-insight index vs bundled, BabyAI A to B: +15.0 vs +9.0 but ALFWorld -2.0 vs +6.5. One item retrieved for 88.5 percent of Task B queries; 13 unique items retrieved (5.4 percent coverage). 200 train and 100 test per phase, 2 runs.
limits: One task pair per environment, one sparse retriever, 2 runs. Some ALFWorld values omitted for fewer than 10 cases.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: abstract or strategy-level records transfer better than raw cases when the target is harder; a sparse index can collapse onto a few hub items.

source: READ-Bench (2026) Benchmarking Historical Instance Retrieval for Time-Series Diagnosis
finding: Retrieval of historical fault cases across 12 diagnostic datasets: shape similarity is a poor proxy for same-fault relevance; pretrained embeddings are no better than classic matching; a small amount of resolved-case labels used to rerank helps most; an LLM reranker adds almost nothing. Without retrieval the LLMs are near random.
numbers: NDCG@10 at 0 percent pollution: random 0.189, DTW 0.480, SAX-BM25 0.489, MantisV2 0.510, best combined system 0.687, supervised reference 0.776. At 20 percent normal-window pollution: best 0.619. LLM classification without retrieval 0.159 to 0.184. LLM rerank on CHARM pool 0.475 to 0.496 vs base 0.486.
limits: Retrieval quality only; no downstream diagnosis accuracy. Time-series signals, not text cases. Read first 100k of 206k characters.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: raw surface similarity indexing is weak in diagnosis; a wrong-fault case can look closer than the right one; stored outcome labels improve retrieval.

source: Stalled, Biased, and Confused (2026) Uncovering Reasoning Failures in LLMs for Cloud-Based Root Cause Analysis
finding: Across 6 open models and 3 workflows (Straight-Shot, ReAct, Plan-and-Execute) the extra agent structure gave no net gain for strong models and hurt small ones. Failures linked to wrong outcomes: anchoring, stalled progress, arbitrary evidence selection, failure to update belief. Self-consistency and domain guidance were recommended but not measured.
numbers: Hypothesis accuracy HA@3, dataset A Straight-Shot / ReAct / Plan-and-Execute: Qwen3-32B 0.36 / 0.35 / 0.30; Llama 3.3 70B 0.29 / 0.31 / 0.29; Qwen3-4B 0.34 / 0.29 / 0.03. Dataset B: Qwen3-32B 0.074 / 0.088 / 0.061. Random 0.06 and 0.004. 3,073 traces judged (about 16 percent of 19,200), kappa 0.92. Mean failures per trace: ReAct 5.1, P&E 4.8, Straight-Shot 4.6.
limits: LLM-judged failure labels; open models only; per-category counts only in a figure.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: a fixed scaffold (agent structure) is not automatically additive even without a case bank; the failures it should block (anchoring, no belief update) match our guardrail targets. Gap 1: self-consistency in RCA was recommended but never measured.

source: PMCoder (2026) Coupling Planning with Episodic Memory in LLM Agents for Software Issue Resolution
finding: Planner and episodic memory are super-additive on SWE-bench Verified: together they gave more than the sum of each alone. The only direct test found of memory interacting with a structured plan (gap 9), on debugging-like issue resolution.
numbers: Qwen3-Coder-30B, 3-run means on 500 issues: baseline 142.33 (28.5 percent), planner only 148.67 (29.7), memory only 150.67 (30.1), both 167.33 (33.5). Interaction +10.3 instances (+2.1 pp), F(1,8)=10.92, p=0.011. Other models single run: DeepSeek-V4-Flash 341 to 357, Claude Haiku 4.5 313 to 327. Token use per arm not reported.
limits: Memory here is the agent's own in-episode history, not a library of past cases. Authors' own method. Harm from misleading memory not measured.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: a plan state that gates what memory is retrieved can be additive or better; not proof for a cross-task case bank. Gap 1: no token-matched control.

source: ReasoningBank (2025) Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory, failure ablation re-check
finding: Re-read. In the failure-case ablation (Gemini-2.5-flash, WebArena-Shopping) 46.5 is the success-only value, not a Pro-table baseline. The no-memory value is 39.0 from table 1. So the a24 concern is resolved: the failure effect is +3.2 for distilled failures, against -2.2 for raw workflow memory.
numbers: Shopping: no memory 39.0; ReasoningBank success only 46.5, with failures 49.7 (+3.2); AWM 44.4 to 42.2 (-2.2); Synapse 40.6 to 41.7 (+1.1). Default retrieval k=1. Judge accuracy of 70 to 90 percent gave similar results.
limits: Figure-7 numbers as read by a summariser from the first 100k of 125k characters; appendix on k ablation and limitations not read. Authors' own paper.
agent_relevance: Corrects a24; the failure-case effect direction stands for distilled lessons.

source: Token-matched memory: synthesis of Cloud-OpsBench, EvoMemBench, Stalled-Biased-Confused, PMCoder
finding: No study found compares a case library with self-consistency or longer reasoning at equal tokens for fault diagnosis. Indirect evidence: memory methods cost more tokens and often lose to a stronger base model; ReasoningBank earlier showed memory plus parallel scaling beats scaling alone; Cloud-OpsBench shows large token jumps buy small accuracy changes.
numbers: EvoMemBench: BM25 memory used 202,966 tokens vs 55,787 for plain DeepSeek on CrossEp-Tool; Cloud-OpsBench Reflection used 76.8K vs ReAct 55.1K for JRA 0.84 vs 0.81 on OB.
limits: Synthesis line, not a new experiment.
agent_relevance: Gap 1 stays open; design the test as case library vs self-consistency with the same total tokens on Cloud-OpsBench.
